summary:
ASTROCARE is a visual health-monitoring prototype designed to help astronauts understand and assess their health during long-duration space missions. We developed a browser-based application featuring a health dashboard, trend charts, an interactive body map, educational guidance, and routine reminders. It presents indicators such as heart rate, sleep duration, and self-reported mood alongside information about spaceflight hazards.

The application also includes an SOS demonstration that allows a crewmate to request assistance and shows who has acknowledged the alert, helping the crew coordinate its response.

ASTROCARE addresses the challenge by making health information accessible through clear visuals and simple explanations, supporting astronauts who carry significant responsibility for monitoring their own well-being. This is particularly important during missions where distance from Earth can delay access to ground support.

Our current prototype uses simulated measurements and educational guidance rather than clinical diagnosis. Future development would focus on sensor integration, reliable communication between crew devices, and validation with medical experts.
details:
ASTROCARE is a health-monitoring prototype designed to help astronauts understand their health, maintain daily routines, and coordinate assistance during space missions.

Features and functionality

The application combines indicators such as heart rate, sleep duration, and self-reported mood in a visual dashboard. Charts display changes over time, while separate sections provide simulated radiation and habitat information.

An interactive body map allows users to select anatomical regions and explore related educational guidance. Reminders support regular health routines, and game elements encourage continued participation.

The SOS feature lets a crewmate request assistance and displays their name, location, and message. A crew response panel shows who needs help, who is responding, and who has not yet acknowledged the alert. It remains visible until the emergency is resolved.

A health-question interface demonstrates conversational support using preset responses. We plan to integrate an AI service for health-related questions and explanations, with expert validation and appropriate limits.

Benefits and intended impact

ASTROCARE aims to make health information easier to understand and help astronauts recognize changes that deserve attention. Combining monitoring, guidance, and emergency coordination is particularly relevant to long missions, where communication delays can limit immediate ground support.

Tools and development

We developed the current prototype using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with local storage and a local communication mechanism for demonstrating SOS alerts. It uses simulated measurements. Future versions would connect suitable wearable sensors and dedicated instruments for radiation and habitat monitoring.

Creativity and team considerations

Our approach combines visual body exploration, game elements, and coordinated emergency responses in one application. During an emergency, the interface prioritizes response information.

Before real mission use, the system would require sensor validation, reliable communication between devices, privacy protections, and medical review. The current prototype provides educational guidance rather than diagnosis.
